PullRequest.Title: Implement Ctrl+F find widget support for chat panes and editors
PullRequest.Body:
This pull request implements the Ctrl+F find widget functionality for the chat pane, chat editors, and the Agents Window in VSCode. The changes include:

- **Shared Find Controller**: A unified implementation for the chat find functionality that serves both the core chat pane and the Agents Window.
- **Transcript Search**: The search now indexes the full logical transcript, including off-screen and collapsed content, ensuring comprehensive search results.
- **UI Enhancements**: Adjustments to the find widget's input box width to match the editor's find widget, including setting `initialWidth: 419` and enabling a draggable sash for user flexibility.
- **Bug Fixes**: Resolved issues related to focus-based commands and incorrect highlighting of search results, ensuring a smoother user experience.

The implementation has been validated with 79 targeted tests passing, and the code has been reviewed for compliance with the approved behavior.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The added outer match loop directly calls _locateMatch; that helper resets each search to the start and constructs all occurrences through occurrenceIndex. The 500-success cap and single animation-frame callback are explicit. Impact magnitude is unmeasured, but the repeated work and allocation count follow directly from the loops.
Findings.PerformanceResource: DOM tree traversals, temporary Range/location objects, regex prefix scans, and editor-model reads/position conversions
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For one mounted part with k successfully located matches, k is capped at 500 per repaint, but prefix matching and range construction grow as k(k+1)/2, plus k full-part DOM walks. Off-screen rows only incur template lookup and are not claimed to be DOM-scanned.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Dropped frames and renderer CPU/GC pressure during search and match navigation
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Chat rendering did not rescan mounted content or create search ranges once per logical occurrence. This entire highlight repaint path is new.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each repaint resolves every logical occurrence separately by rebuilding its part's text, rerunning the regex from the beginning, constructing the entire matching prefix, and then discarding all but one location.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added lines 519-520 invoke _locateMatch once per match. Added lines 474-482 call findMatchRangesInDom and findMatchRangesInCodeBlock with occurrenceIndex + 1; both helpers reset regex.lastIndex to zero. The DOM helper walks the complete root before matching.
Findings.Title: Locate each rendered part's matches once per repaint
Findings.Impact: Searching a common word or short identifier in a long response/code sample makes typing and match navigation janky; keeping Find open also adds this work after debounced transcript updates.
Findings.Evidence: For k matches in one mounted markdown part, occurrence 0 constructs one range, occurrence 1 constructs two, and so on. With the advertised 500 visible highlights this creates 125250 temporary DOM ranges and walks the same root 500 times in one repaint, despite retaining only 500 ranges. Code matches similarly repeat prefix scans and position conversions; findMatchRangesInCodeBlock additionally calls model.getValue() inside its regex loop. _revealActiveMatch runs this synchronously in an animation-frame callback after query changes and Next/Previous, and content updates also schedule it.
Findings.Recommendation: Group matches by mounted row/part and compute its ordered DOM/code locations once per repaint, bounded by the required highlight budget; reuse that list for occurrences. Snapshot each code model's text outside the regex loop.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: SimpleFindWidget's input listener synchronously invokes the new setQuery/recompute path. buildSegments traverses every item, and the shared plaintext helper synchronously parses and sanitizes every markdown part. Response dataId provides an existing revision signal. Only the transcript sizes and resulting duration are uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Synchronous markdown parsing, DOM sanitization, annotation work, and transient plaintext/segment allocations
Findings.PerformanceScaling: With Q query edits or fired content debounces and transcript size T, expensive plaintext extraction repeats Q times over T, even when only the query or one live response changes. Each markdown part is bounded at 100000 parsed characters, but the number of parts/responses is not bounded by the match cap.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased Find input latency and renderer CPU/GC pressure as conversation history grows
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Normal chat rendering processed mounted rows; the accessible-view plaintext extraction operated on its focused response. There was no whole-history plaintext reconstruction for every Find keystroke or transcript update.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every nonempty query change and each debounced content recomputation re-annotates and re-extracts all responses, including unchanged completed and virtualized responses, before regex matching starts.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 217 unconditionally calls buildSegments(this.getItems()). Added buildSegments lines 61-76 iterate the full transcript and invoke annotateSpecialMarkdownContentWithSource and getChatResponsePlaintextParts for every response. setQuery calls recompute directly, and ChatFindWidget._onInputChanged invokes setQuery synchronously.
Findings.Title: Reuse extracted transcript segments across query changes
Findings.Impact: In long coding/agent conversations with many completed responses, typing in Find blocks the UI on repeated markdown parsing and sanitization of unchanged history. Leaving Find open also makes updates to the latest response reprocess the entire history.
Findings.Evidence: getChatResponsePlaintextParts calls renderAsPlaintext for markdown and markdown-valued tool messages. markdownRenderer.ts:710-727 runs marked.parse with async:false followed by DOM sanitization, with a 100000-character cap per markdown part, not per transcript. This work repeats on every query character without a cache; the 9999-match limit is checked only after all segments have already been built. Content changes are debounced by 200 ms, but still rebuild completed history after each fired debounce. ChatResponseViewModel.dataId includes its model-change counter and changes on content updates.
Findings.Recommendation: Retain extracted segments per response revision, for example keyed by item identity and dataId. Reuse them for query/options changes, rebuild only changed responses, and prune entries on item removal or session replacement.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: Static trace establishes the Unicode regex, one-code-unit advancement, rejected node-boundary ranges, and limit based only on accepted ranges. The existing Searcher in textModelSearch.ts:529-539 explicitly handles surrogate pairs to avoid this failure; no timing assumption is needed.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Renderer-thread regex executions and DOM range-location attempts
Findings.PerformanceScaling: A single affected formatted response is sufficient: the same rejected zero-length match repeats without advancing, so execution is unbounded even with the visible-highlight limit.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Unbounded renderer CPU work and an unresponsive application window
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Chat did not execute this new DOM regex loop when searching the transcript; the editor's existing Searcher advances empty matches safely across surrogate pairs.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new DOM search increments lastIndex by one UTF-16 code unit after an empty match and only stops after enough valid DOM ranges have been accumulated.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added lines 107-118 call regex.exec(buffer), discard undefined toDomRange results, increment lastIndex by one, and test ranges.length rather than iterations. _tryCreateRegex enables unicode at line 428, and the added repaint loop invokes this helper with increasing occurrence limits.
Findings.Title: Advance zero-length regex matches by Unicode code point
Findings.Impact: Using the ordinary zero-width regex `\b` in a transcript containing formatted text immediately followed by an emoji can permanently occupy the renderer thread, freezing the window until it is reloaded.
Findings.Evidence: For a response containing markdown `**hi**😀`, the rendered inline text nodes produce buffer `hi😀` with node spans [0,2] and [2,4]. Regex `\b` matches offsets 0 and 2. At 2, toDomRange selects the second node for the start and the first for the end, returning undefined. Incrementing lastIndex to 3 enters the emoji's low surrogate; a Unicode regex resumes at 2 and returns the same empty boundary indefinitely. When repaint locates the second occurrence with limit 2, only the offset-0 range counts, so the loop never terminates. The logical model's separate 9999-match cap does not bound this DOM loop.
Findings.Recommendation: Use Unicode-aware zero-length advancement, preferably the existing Searcher, consistently in the DOM, logical-model, and code-block loops. Ensure progress is independent of whether toDomRange accepts a match.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create and display chat panes, chat editors, and Agents Window chats with Find closed; close or replace these widgets, including split chats.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Widget rendering constructs a SimpleFindWidget, model, context keys, and listeners. Empty queries exit before transcript extraction, and Find content listeners gate recomputation on visibility. Ordinary row rendering still calls the shared annotation helper, which now also constructs source-index metadata.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One Find controller per enabled chat widget; ordinary annotation metadata scales with response content parts. Quick/inline chat do not opt in.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: UI-thread construction and rendering. Each widget owns its own scheduler and delayer; no new subprocess, IPC, database, or network work is initiated by constructing Find.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No transcript index is built while Find is unused. The shared per-window highlight registry uses a WeakMap; owner ranges are removed on hide/dispose. Code-decoration entries are cleared and removed, and timers/listeners are registered for disposal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in visibility gates, ownership, and cleanup from constructor/hide/dispose paths.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Startup cost of the fixed-size widget and annotation metadata allocation was not profiled.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional high-confidence finding for hidden-widget allocation or cleanup. The added UI is fixed-size per widget, and lifecycle cleanup is present. The annotation refactor adds temporary metadata, but a separate material regression beyond existing merging costs was not established.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open transcript Find and type or change search options in a long completed conversation.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: SimpleFindWidget's input listener synchronously invokes ChatFindWidget._onInputChanged -> ChatFindModel.setQuery -> recompute -> buildSegments over all logical rows. Regex matching starts only after all segments are extracted. Navigation/highlighting is scheduled afterward.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronous marked parsing followed by DOM sanitization to derive plaintext.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Each applicable markdown response/tool-message part in the entire transcript is parsed again on every nonempty query edit or options recomputation. Parsing is capped at 100000 characters per markdown part, not per conversation; the 9999-match cap is applied afterward.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Accessible View extracted plaintext for its focused response, and ordinary rendering processed mounted rows. There was no whole-transcript extraction on Find input.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously before the input handler returns; no network or file reads are needed for plaintext extraction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: JSON.stringify of structured tool rawInput and construction/joining of tool description strings.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once for each applicable structured input tool description visited during each full extraction, subject to the tool-state branch; query edits repeat it for unchanged history.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same formatter was used by Accessible View for one focused response, rather than repeatedly across the transcript during Find typing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous CPU/allocation on the Find input path; no tool execution or external request is performed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total logical transcript text, number of response/tool-message parts, structured tool-input sizes, and number of query edits. Virtualization does not reduce extraction cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serial renderer-thread work, without input debouncing or worker offload. Match storage is capped at 9999, but extraction is not bounded by that cap.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no segment/plaintext cache: cold and warm query edits both re-annotate and re-extract unchanged responses. Existing response dataId exposes a revision signal suitable for invalidation. Empty or invalid queries return before extraction.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: direct input call chain, full traversal, parser/sanitizer implementation, and missing reuse are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Conversation sizes and parsing durations vary; no benchmark duration is asserted.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported repeated whole-transcript plaintext reconstruction as an introduced input-latency regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Keep Find open while the latest agent response streams or tool state changes, or switch the displayed session.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Response model changes propagate through ChatResponseViewModel and ChatViewModel into ChatWidget's accumulated content event. The Find listener restarts a 200 ms trailing Delayer. Each executed callback synchronously rebuilds all segments, updates matches, and schedules highlighting.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Re-extract and sanitize plaintext for completed history as well as the changed live response.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full-transcript extraction per fired trailing debounce, not one per token. Events continuously arriving faster than the debounce coalesce until a gap; separate sufficiently spaced updates each cause another full extraction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Streaming did not invoke the new logical transcript search rebuild across completed history.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Deferred off the model event's immediate stack, but the executed extraction still occupies the renderer thread and competes with response rendering and input.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Regenerate structured tool-input and description strings during the rebuild.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The applicable tool parts across history are serialized once per fired full rebuild, including unchanged completed tools.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No transcript-wide Find serialization occurred on live model changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Part of the synchronous delayed extraction; no subprocess or tool/network execution is triggered.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Completed transcript size multiplied by fired debounce callbacks, plus the changing response's size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Content bursts are coalesced by one Delayer per widget. Each executed rebuild is serial, followed by a coalesced animation-frame repaint; this is not per-token parallel fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The active-match anchor is retained, but extracted text is not. Find hide cancels the delayer, and disposal owns it. Session replacement uses the host's current item list.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: model-event propagation and trailing debounce implementation were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: How often real streams leave 200 ms gaps and the size of completed histories are workload-dependent.
Scenarios.Verdict: Same extraction root cause as the reported segment-reuse finding, with the debounce correctly accounted for; no duplicate finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Highlight and navigate matches in mounted text/code, or reveal an off-screen response and expand completed-response disclosures.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Next/Previous or a query change selects a logical match, reveals its single chat item through the existing virtualized list, and schedules _revealActiveMatch. Match location, optional disclosure expansion, scrolling, and highlight repaint occur on the renderer thread. Expansion may schedule one additional frame.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Walk DOM roots, recreate text buffers and matching prefixes, allocate DOM/editor ranges, and read embedded code models.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most 500 successfully located highlights per repaint, but each occurrence independently rescans its part through occurrenceIndex. For 500 matches in one mounted plain-text part, this means 500 full DOM walks and 125250 temporary DOM ranges. Up to 9999 logical matches may receive cheap template lookups; off-screen rows are not DOM-scanned.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous work inside the animation-frame callback delays painting and subsequent interaction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing markdown row rendering can insert image elements and load their resources when Find reveals an unmounted row.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Loads scale with permitted images in newly mounted rows, not with the number of logical matches. Already mounted rows and browser resource caches can eliminate additional requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Manual scrolling/revealing the same row used the same renderer and image-loading behavior. The diff newly routes Find navigation through that existing reveal path, without eager transcript-wide image loads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Image loading is asynchronous and is not awaited by Find's regex search or initial range lookup; later load callbacks may affect row layout.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create/reuse embedded code editors and in-memory text models for code blocks in mounted rows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing editor pools serve mounted code blocks; cold construction creates local models/references per needed pooled editor, not per Find match. Highlight searches then access already mounted models synchronously.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same editor pools and local model creation were used when manually revealing those rows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold row rendering contributes to reveal cost; these code-block model references do not require filesystem or network reads.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Conditional existing file/remote-file model resolution when a revealed response contains text-edit comparisons and summary rendering is disabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One original-model reference per rendered text-edit comparison, coalesced by canonical URI in the shared asynchronous reference collection; each modified comparison model is local. Core chat/editor hosts enable summary rendering and skip this path; the Agents host does not set that summary option.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Manually revealing the same row performed the same conditional model resolutions. Find adds a navigation entry point, not per-match file resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Comparison model resolution is asynchronous; Find does not await all comparison files before searching or selecting a row. Existing row contents may finish rendering later.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Successfully located matches per mounted part, part DOM/model size, number of newly mounted row resources, and query/navigation/update frequency.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One renderer-thread repaint callback at a time; each part's match scans are serial. Existing image loads and conditional file resolutions can proceed asynchronously for newly mounted content, not for all transcript matches.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Frame scheduling coalesces repaint requests, but locations are not reused even within a repaint. Template lookup rejects unmounted/recycled rows. Editor pooling, canonical-URI model reference sharing, and browser image caching remain intact.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both highlight loops, template ownership, editor pools, and conditional model-resolution paths were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact frame costs and rich-row resource counts vary; the temporary-range count is a static loop count, not a measured benchmark.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported quadratic per-occurrence location work. Existing resource loading on row reveal does not independently establish a boundary-fan-out regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Use a zero-width regex such as \b against formatted response text immediately followed by an emoji.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The logical model builds a bounded match set, then the animation-frame repaint repeatedly locates occurrences in rendered DOM. The DOM regex loop must finish before the frame and subsequent UI events can proceed.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: A single response containing markdown **hi** followed immediately by an emoji is sufficient; its two inline text nodes create a zero-width node-boundary match before a surrogate pair.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A synchronous infinite loop on the renderer thread; there is no cancellation yield, worker, or asynchronous boundary.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each location scan resets the Unicode regex to zero. Rejected DOM ranges do not increment the result-based limit, and no progress guard or cached location prevents retrying the same empty boundary.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced UTF-16 node spans, toDomRange rejection, Unicode lastIndex rewind, and accepted-range-only termination; the existing editor Searcher explicitly implements surrogate-aware empty-match progress.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The input combination is less common than ordinary text search, but the nontermination mechanism is independent of transcript size or machine speed.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported Unicode-unsafe empty-match advancement causing an unbounded CPU loop and frozen window. The separate 9999 logical-match cap and 500 successful-highlight cap do not bound this rejected-range loop.

Scenarios.Scenario: Read a response in Accessible View, open Chat Find accessibility help, and use multiple independent Find widgets.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Accessible View still extracts one focused response and normalizes its text. Find help builds a fixed-size help string. Focus routing searches existing widgets and dispatches to one controller.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Plaintext extraction and sanitization for the focused response.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One focused response per Accessible View content request, as before; the refactor adds part wrappers and a map/join but does not expand the accessible-view extraction to the entire transcript.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same content kinds were parsed and joined for the focused response before helper extraction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous content generation, with unchanged parsing scope.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Focused-response size for Accessible View; number of open widgets for focus lookup; fixed help content size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serial UI-thread focus dispatch to one controller. Separate visible widgets do not multiply a single Find command into searches across all chats.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Storage-backed include-thinking preference remains a synchronous cached service read. Each controller owns its model/context keys; the per-window highlight registry merges at most its owners' supplied ranges and clears disposed owners.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: before/after extraction, focused-item provider, command resolution, and registry cleanup were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No meaningful unbounded/scaling amplification was established on these auxiliary paths.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional high-confidence performance regression in accessibility extraction, command routing, or shared-highlight ownership.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all 27 changed files and all diff pages against base ad20a3de974992acd6377bb5085fc3590541c74d. Submitted three introduced regressions: Unicode zero-width DOM-search nontermination, quadratic per-occurrence highlight reconstruction, and repeated full-transcript plaintext extraction. Examined visibility/lifecycle, input and streaming scheduling, virtualization, code-model reads, conditional file resolution, image loading, serialization, accessibility, and multi-widget ownership. No concrete pre-existing performance regression fix qualified for blame provenance collection. Static read-only review; no runtime timings are asserted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
